Adding a digital version of a driver's license to iPhone looks set to expand to the 15th U.S. state in the near future.

Apple currently lists 14 states that support the feature, along with the territory of Puerto Rico, but backend assets indicate one more state will be added to the list...

Many of us have long hoped for the day when we wouldn't need to carry physical identification documents such as driver's licenses and passports, and could simply present digital ID through our iPhone or Apple Watch.

That future may still be some way off, but Apple took its first step back in 2021, when it announced plans to let iPhone users add driver's licenses or state IDs to the Wallet app. To date, 14 states have adopted the feature:

  • Arizona
  • Arkansas
  • California
  • Colorado
  • Georgia
  • Hawaii
  • Illinois
  • Iowa
  • Maryland
  • Montana
  • New Mexico
  • North Dakota
  • Ohio
  • West Virginia

According to backend assets discovered by MacRumors, Oklahoma will soon be added to the list.

We previously outlined the steps for adding a driver's license or state ID to the Wallet app on iPhone. As noted at the time, bear in mind that digital ID cannot fully replace physical documents, so unfortunately we still recommend carrying the "slimmed-down" physical document with you.

That said, the digital version can help protect your privacy at eligible TSA checkpoints and when you need to prove your age to merchants. The system will only confirm that you meet the age requirement, without disclosing any personal information such as your date of birth.
